question.problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the finite solid region enclosed by the planes $x=0,$ $x=1,$ $z=0,$ $z=1,$ and the surfaces $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=x-z+2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=z\,i-4y\,j+{z}^{3}\,k,$ the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS=

question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{3}) \\  & =0-4+3{z}^{2} \\  & =3{z}^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}(3{z}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type III solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x-z+2\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(3{z}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x-z+2}\,3{z}^{2}-4\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
